snippet.title: 8 Times Earth Almost Died: The Worst Days in the Planet's History
snippet.description: Life on Earth has come to the very edge of total extinction more than once. This is a countdown of the eight worst catastrophes our planet has ever endured — from the day oxygen itself became a poison, to the planet freezing solid pole to pole, to the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs, to the supervolcano that nearly wiped out the human race. Eight times the thread of life was pulled so thin it almost snapped. Drawn from the layers in the rock where the fossils stop, the ash buried in the ice, and the faint chemical scars deep time leaves behind. We have survived eight near-endings to be here. How many more can the Earth take? Tell us what you believe in the comments.

snippet.title: Snowball Earth: When the Entire Planet Turned to Ice
snippet.description: Seven hundred million years ago, the whole Earth froze solid — ice from pole to pole, glaciers grinding to the sea at the equator, the oceans frozen more than a kilometre deep. This is the story of Snowball Earth: how a living world tipped into the deepest cold it has ever known, how the thread of life survived beneath the ice for millions of years, and how the violent thaw that followed may have lit the fuse for all complex life — including us. Drawn from glacier-ground rock found today at the tropics, where no glacier should ever have reached, and the strange chemistry frozen into the stone. If it happened once, could the whole world freeze again? Tell us what you believe in the comments.

snippet.title: The Great Dying: The Worst Extinction in Earth's History
snippet.description: Two hundred and fifty-two million years ago, life on Earth came closer to ending than at any other moment in its history. This is the story of the Great Dying — the slow, suffocating catastrophe that killed ninety-six percent of life in the sea and seven in ten on the land, not in a single day, but over thousands of years, poisoned from within by the Earth itself. Drawn from the lava that buried a land the size of a continent in Siberia, and from the layer in the rock where, almost everywhere on Earth, the fossils simply stop. The planet has come close to ending its own life once. Could it happen again? Tell us what you believe in the comments.

snippet.title: The Zanclean Flood: The Megaflood That Refilled the Mediterranean
snippet.description: Five and a half million years ago, the Mediterranean Sea vanished. Cut off from the Atlantic, it dried until it was a sunken desert of salt and brine, almost two miles below the level of the world ocean — the deepest, hottest, deadest place on the face of the Earth. And then, in a single geological instant, the Atlantic broke through. This is the story of the Zanclean Flood: the largest flood in the history of our planet, a waterfall a thousand times the size of the Amazon, refilling an entire sea in a matter of months. Drawn from the salt buried beneath the seabed, the drowned canyons carved into the rock, and the strange chemistry frozen into the stone. If a sea can die and be reborn once, what does that say about the ones we know? Tell us what you believe in the comments.

snippet.title: Yellowstone: The Supervolcano That Already Erupted Three Times
snippet.description: Beneath the geysers and forests of Yellowstone lies one of the most powerful volcanoes on the face of the Earth — a supervolcano that has already erupted three times, burying half a continent in ash. This is the story of what sleeps under Yellowstone: the vast chamber of molten rock that drives it, the three colossal eruptions written into the rock, the trail of dead craters it has left across the American west, and the truth about whether it is really "overdue" to erupt again. Drawn from the ash layers buried across the continent, the slow breathing of the ground, and the deep scans that let us see beneath the surface. One day, it will wake. The only question the rock cannot answer is when. Tell us what you believe in the comments.

snippet.title: The Last Day of the Dinosaurs: The Asteroid They Never Saw Coming
snippet.description: Sixty-six million years ago, on an ordinary morning, a rock ten kilometres wide fell out of the sky and ended the age of the dinosaurs in a single day. This is the story of the worst day in the history of life on Earth — the impact, the firestorm, the years of darkness that followed, and the small, frightened survivors in the burrows that would one day become us. Drawn from the buried Chicxulub crater, the thin grey line of ash and rare metal found in the rock all over the world, and the bones that simply stop at that line. Was the asteroid the end of the world, or the beginning of ours? Tell us what you believe in the comments.

snippet.title: 10 Prehistoric Disasters That Almost Ended Humanity
snippet.description: Long before history was written, the planet tried to kill us — and ten times it very nearly succeeded. From the supervolcano that shrank the entire human species to a few thousand survivors, to the flood that refilled an empty sea in a single human lifetime, these are the ten prehistoric catastrophes that came within a breath of erasing the human race forever. Cinematic recreation. Numbers and dates are best-current-estimate from the geological and archaeological record.
